rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رسول may be an adjective meaning “sent,” on the فعول pattern like صبور and شكور.
rows.anchor: صفة بمعنى مرسل فهو صفة على فعول كالصبور والشكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رسول may also be a verbal noun meaning “message”; the anonymous cited poem uses برسول in this sense.
rows.anchor: بسر ولا أرسلتهم برسول أي: برسالة، وقال آخر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second anonymous poem likewise uses رسولا for a message delivered to Abu Salma.
rows.anchor: أبلغ أبا سلمى رسولا تروعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one interpretation, the Qur’anic رسول means bearer of a message from the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: على أحد التأولين، أي: إنا ذوا رسالة رب العالمين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري وابن عطية
rows.claim: If رسول is an adjective, it may coordinate with يعلمه, itself read as a circumstantial phrase coordinated with وجيها.
rows.anchor: قاله الزمخشري وابن عطية

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Sheikh calls that parse weak because it depends on the already weak coordination of ويعلمه with وجيها across a long separation.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهو مبني على إعراب " ويعلمه " ، وقد بينا ضعف إعراب

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya allows رسول to coordinate with كهلا, the circumstantial phrase attached to يكلم.
rows.anchor: جوز ذلك ابن عطية. واستبعده الشيخ

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Sheikh considers coordination with كهلا remote because of the long distance between the coordinated terms.
rows.anchor: استبعده الشيخ لطول الفصل بين المعطوف والمعطوف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects this parse on meaning: it would make Jesus speak to people as their messenger before he became a messenger, years later.
rows.anchor: وهو إنما صار رسولا بعد ذلك بأزمنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A future circumstantial state can be allowed when unambiguous, as in the falcon example and 39:73; the default circumstantial state is simultaneous.
rows.anchor: الأصل في الحال أن تكون مقارنة، ولا تكون مقدرة إلا حيث لا لبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse supplies the suitable verb ونجعله because رسول cannot coordinate directly with the preceding teaching objects; examples elide verbs before faith, spear, water, and eyes.
rows.anchor: تقديره: ونجعله رسولا، لما رأوه لا يصح عطفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted-verb examples continue with implied “believe” before faith, “carry” before spear, “water” before cold water, and “apply kohl to” before eyes.
rows.anchor: أي: واعتقدوا الإيمان، ومعتقلا رمحا، وسقيتها ماء باردا، وكحلن العيون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth parse supplies a verb derived from رسول, itself governed by an omitted speech verb attributed to Jesus.
rows.anchor: منصوبا بإضمار فعل من لفظ " رسول " ، ويكون ذلك الفعل معمولا لقول مضمر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari proposes supplying أرسلت under implicit speech: Jesus says he was sent as a messenger who came with the message and affirms earlier scripture.
rows.anchor: ما قاله الزمخشري، قاله رحمه الله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Alternatively رسول and مصدقا imply speech, yielding “uttering that I have come to you” and affirming what came before.
rows.anchor: فيهما معنى النطق، فكأنه قيل: وناطقا بأني قد جئتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elisions reconcile the prior third-person pronouns with first-person pronouns in these phrases and make the syntax and meaning consistent.
rows.anchor: من المنصوبات لا يصح عطفه عليه في الظاهر

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Sheikh rejects the two-elision proposal as weak and redundant: an omitted saying and أرسلت are unnecessary when رسول already means messenger.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهذا الوجه ضعيف؛ إذ فيه إضمار شيئين: القول ومعموله

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Sheikh prefers the third parse because it requires only one omitted verb and lets أني قد جئتكم complement رسول as speech on the majority reading.
rows.anchor: واختار الشيخ الوجه الثالث قال: " إذ ليس فيه إلا إضمار فعل يدل عليه المعنى

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash makes رسول a circumstantial phrase from the object of ويعلمه, assuming و is redundant.
rows.anchor: قاله الأخفش، وهذا على أصل مذهبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls redundant و a weak position in keeping with al-Akhfash’s grammatical doctrine.
rows.anchor: وهذا على أصل مذهبه من تجويزه زيادة الواو، وهو مذهب مرجوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If رسول is a verbal noun, it may be a direct object coordinated with the second object of يعلمه, meaning Jesus is taught the message too.
rows.anchor: عطفا على المفعول الثاني ليعلمه أي: ويعلمه الكتاب ورسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If رسول is a verbal noun, it may instead function as a circumstantial verbal noun, with the familiar interpretation of رجل عدل.
rows.anchor: أنه مصدر في موضع الحال، وفيه التأويلات المشهورة في: رجل عدل

rows.speaker: اليزيدي
rows.claim: Al-Yazidi reads رسول in the genitive, and al-Zamakhshari links it to بكلمة as two objects of glad tidings; the author finds the long separation awkward but sees no clearer parse.
rows.anchor: قرأ اليزيدي: " ورسول " بالجر، وخرجها الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلى بني إسرائيل may be governed by رسول, whose verb takes إلى, or may be an omitted adjective modifying رسول.
rows.anchor: يتعدى بإلى، والثاني: أن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنه صفة لرسولا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority opens the hamza of أني; a genitive parse deletes ب, making the phrase dependent on رسول, as al-Khalil and al-Kisaʾi hold.
rows.anchor: وهذا مذهب الشيخين: الخليل والكسائي

rows.speaker: سيبويه والفراء
rows.claim: For the open-hamza reading, Sibawayh and al-Farraʾ parse أني accusative after deleting the preposition ب.
rows.anchor: وهذا مذهب التلميذين: سيبويه والفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another accusative parse supplies يذكر, with the phrase left as its complement after its modifying phrase for رسول is omitted.
rows.anchor: فيذكر صفة لرسولا، حذفت الصفة وبقي معمولها

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ allows أني as an accusative substitute for رسول when رسول is a verbal noun direct object; the author finds this semantically remote.
rows.anchor: جوزه أبو البقاء وهو بعيد في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parse gives the open-hamza phrase nominative as predicate of an omitted subject: هو أني قد جئتكم.
rows.anchor: أي: هو أني قد جئتكم

rows.speaker: بعض القراء
rows.claim: Some reciters break the hamza; one parse supplies omitted قول with a circumstantial قائلا, retaining its complement.
rows.anchor: قرأ بعض القراء بكسر هذه الهمزة وفيها تأويلان

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans explain the broken hamza by taking رسول as “speaker,” embedding the meaning and syntax of saying.
rows.anchor: أعطي حكم القول، وهذا مذهب الكوفيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بآية may be an omitted-predicate circumstantial phrase describing Jesus as coming accompanied by a sign, or attach directly to the coming.
rows.anchor: جئتكم ملتبسا بآية. والثاني: أنها متعلقة بنفس المجيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من ربكم may modify آية through an omitted عند, with من marking figurative origin, or may attach directly to the coming.
rows.anchor: أي: بآية من عند ربكم

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ estimates the circumstantial meaning as “advancing with a sign”; the author accepts this semantically but not as formal syntax.
rows.anchor: بقوله: محتجا بآية، إن عنى من جهة المعنى صح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For grammatical ellipsis, the author says only an absolute existential verb is supplied, not the specific verb محتجا.
rows.anchor: لم يضمر في هذه الأماكن إلا الأكوان المطلقة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: The majority reads آية in the singular in both occurrences; Ibn Masʿud reads آيات in the plural both times.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور: " بآية " بالإفراد في الموضعين، وابن مسعود

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafiʿ breaks the hamza of أني أخلق; the other readers open it.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع بكسر الهمزة، والباقون بفتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With Nafiʿ’s reading, the phrase may follow an omitted saying, resume independently, or explain what the sign is; explanatory usage remains linked to آية, unlike pure resumption.
rows.anchor: على إضمار القول أي: فقلت: إني أخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanatory reading is illustrated by 3:59, where خلقه من تراب explains the likeness, and 5:9, where لهم مغفرة explains the promise.
rows.anchor: فخلقه مفسرة للمثل، ونظيره أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the majority’s open hamza, the phrase may substitute for أني قد جئتكم or for آية as a statement that is itself a sign.
rows.anchor: بدل من " آية " فتكون محلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively it may be predicate of an omitted subject هي, answering the implied question, “What is the sign?”
rows.anchor: الثالث: أنها خبر مبتدأ مضمر تقديره: هي أني أخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final parse supplies أعني as its governing verb, likewise answering the implied question about the sign.
rows.anchor: منصوبة بإضمار فعل، وهو أيضا جواب لذلك السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لكم attaches to أخلق; the lām expresses purpose: securing the audience’s faith and ending denial, since people themselves are not ends but their actions are.
rows.anchor: واللام للعلة، أي: لأجلكم بمعنى: لتحصيل إيمانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من الطين attaches to أخلق and marks starting material; calling من explanatory is lax because no prior phrase needs clarification.
rows.anchor: إذ لم يسبق منهم تبينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred parse makes the comparison an adjective of an omitted object: Jesus creates an object whose form resembles a bird’s form.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أنها نعت لمفعول محذوف تقديره: أني أخلق لكم هيئة مثل هيئة الطير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هيئة can be a verbal noun transferred to its result, like خلق for created thing, or a noun for a thing’s state; verbal nouns include التهيؤ and التهيئة.
rows.anchor: وإما اسم لحال الشيء، وليست مصدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root هاء الشيء يهيء describes something arranged and settled in a particular state; the Qur’an uses يهيئ لكم in 18:16.
rows.anchor: هاء الشيء يهيء هيئا وهيئة إذا ترتب واستقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طانه الله على كذا and variant طامه mean God fashioned him that way, with ن replaced by م; blowing is familiar usage.
rows.anchor: طانه الله على كذا وطامه بإبدال النون ميما

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash treats kaf itself as the direct object because he regards it as a noun wherever it occurs; other grammarians allow this only under necessity.
rows.anchor: وهذا رأي الأخفش، يجعل الكاف اسما حيث وقعت

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi, transmitting from Abu ʿAli, parses kaf as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, “a creating like a bird’s form.”
rows.anchor: قاله الواحدي نقلا عن أبي علي بعد كلام طويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that the challenge concerns the created result, not creating itself, unless the verbal noun means its object, returning to the first parse.
rows.anchor: لأن التحدي إنما يقع في أثر الخلق، وهو ما ينشأ عنه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari paraphrases أخلق as أقدر, clarifying that human “creation” here means measuring or shaping.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " إني أقدر لكم شيئا مثل هيئة الطير "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anonymous poetic line uses يخلق for estimating or fashioning, not origination, which is exclusive to God.
rows.anchor: إذ ليس المراد الاختراع فإنه مختص بالباري تعالى

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri reads كهية by moving the hamza’s vowel to yāʾ, a form the author calls eloquent.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري: " كهية " بنقل حركة الهمزة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads كهيئة الطائر in place of كهيئة الطير.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: كهيئة الطائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun فيه has six proposed antecedents: kaf; هيئة understood as a shaped thing; an omitted object; the created thing implied by أخلق; the comparison sense of kaf; or clay.
rows.anchor: في هذا الضمير ستة أوجه، أحدها: أنه عائد على الكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the هيئة parse, the pronoun is masculine by sense (“thing shaped”), despite the feminine word; 4:8 similarly returns منه to القسمة meaning the divided property.
rows.anchor: لأنها في معنى الشيء المهيأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses return فيه to the omitted object, the created result implied by أخلق, or the comparison sense of kaf.
rows.anchor: أنه عائد على ذلك المفعول المحذوف أي: فأنفخ في ذلك الشيء

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli returns the pronoun to the comparison sense of kaf, with kaf describing an omitted verbal noun: creating a creation like a bird’s form.
rows.anchor: قاله الفارسي وقد تقدم الكلام معه في ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ returns فيه to الطين; al-Wahidi objects that the blowing is into fashioned clay, not the general clay mentioned earlier.
rows.anchor: قاله أبو البقاء. وهذا الوجه قد أفسده الواحدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author counters that من may partitivize the clay, allowing the pronoun to refer to that portion; al-Wahidi instead takes من as marking origin, which the author calls more apparent.
rows.anchor: بل المراد بعضه، ولذلك أدخل عليه

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Sheikh mentions a rare فأنفخها reading; feminine agreement refers to an omitted هيئة or to kaf by its feminine sense, as in 5:110.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وقد قرأ بعض القراء: " فأنفخها " أعاد الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine reading omits في: an unnamed poet’s نائحة did not rise for someone, and al-Nabigha’s line means “blows into the coal.”
rows.anchor: ما شق جيب ولا قامتك نائحة ولا بكتك جياد عند إسلاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha’s phrase ينفخ الفحما omits في, meaning “blows into the coal,” just as the feminine reading omits its preposition.
rows.anchor: يريد: ولا قامت عليك، وينفخ في الفحم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ transmits فأنفخها as rare; al-Kashshaf attributes it to ʿAbd Allah, a detail the author says al-Farraʾ omitted.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة شاذة نقلها الفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يكون may be complete, with طيرا circumstantial, or incomplete with طيرا as predicate; the author prefers incomplete syntax because a bare species noun is awkward as a circumstantial.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنها تامة أي: فيوجد

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ says يكون means يصير and permits complete or incomplete syntax; with طائرا the first has a circumstantial and the second a predicate.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " فيكون " أي: يصير، فيجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says complete كان needs no “become” sense: grammarians mean حدث or وجد; صار meaning “become” is defective.
rows.anchor: النحويون إنما يقدرون التامة بمعنى حدث ووجد وحصل

rows.speaker: نافع ويعقوب
rows.claim: Nafiʿ and Yaʿqub read فيكون طائرا here and in 5:110; the remaining readers have طيرا in both places.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع ويعقوب: " فيكون طائرا "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular can mean each thing Jesus breathes into becomes a bird; omission of alif in the codex is permissible, as 6:38 writes طير for recited طائر.
rows.anchor: الرسم الكريم إنما هو " طير " دون ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of Nafiʿ’s singular is that Jesus created only one kind of bird, the bat; another says each form he breathes into becomes a bird, like the distributive “eighty lashes” in 24:4.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم كالشارح لما قدمته

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: For the majority’s طيرا, al-Akhfash regards طير as a plural form like ركب, صحب, and تجر; Sibawayh calls these collective nouns rather than explicit plurals.
rows.anchor: جمع راكب وصاحب وتاجر وهو الأخفش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reading may mean the bird species, one bird, or many; the author favors it for matching من الطير and the written form and sense.
rows.anchor: ولموافقة الرسم لفظا ومعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Nafiʿ’s طائرا reading, بإذن الله may modify طائرا; with collective طيرا it is an adjective of the bird phrase through an omitted relation, meaning enabled by God.
rows.anchor: وهذا على قراءة نافع، وأما على قراءة غيره فلا يتعلق به

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ attaches the phrase to يكون; this appears only if كان is complete, while attachment to a defective verb is disputed.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " متعلق بيكون "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وأبرئ coordinates with أخلق, so it remains within the scope of أني.
rows.anchor: فهو داخل في حيز " أني "

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿi assigns برئت من المرض to Tamim and برأت to the Hijaz; al-Raghib infers both vowels apply to illness, while debt and sin take fatḥa only.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: " برئت من المرض لغة تميم وبرأت لغة الحجاز "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms include أبرأت someone from illness or debt, برأتك from debt with doubled rāʾ, and برئت من المرض for recovery; البراءة means escaping a disliked thing, as do التبري and البرء.
rows.anchor: أبرأت زيدا من العاهة ومن الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأكمه can mean one born blind, from كمه يكمه; the author cites Ruʾba’s line using the word.
rows.anchor: كمه يكمه كمها فهو أكمه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري والراغب
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and al-Raghib define الأكمه as one born with eyes extinguished; al-Zamakhshari says Qatada was the only such person in this community.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري والراغب وغيرهما: " الأكمه من ولد مطموس العين "

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib also allows الأكمه for someone whose eyes were lost, citing Suwayd’s line كمهت عيناه.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب: " وقد يقال لمن ذهبت عينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: البرص is the familiar disease of white patches, also called الوضح; Arabs particularly recoiled from it, and the author gives its root verb.
rows.anchor: والبرص داء معروف وهو بياض يعتري الإنسان، ولم تكن العرب تنفر من شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report وكان بها وضح illustrates الوضح; an Arab king was called الوضاح because people avoided calling him الأبرص, and the moon is also called أبرص for whiteness.
rows.anchor: والوضاح من ملوك العرب هابوا أن يقولوا له الأبرص

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib attributes the moon’s name أبرص to its spot, but the author objects that the spot is black.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب: " للنكتة التي عليه " وليس بظاهر، فإن النكتة التي عليه سوداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lizard is called سام أبرص because of its whiteness; تبريص describes a gleam resembling the shine of leprosy.
rows.anchor: والوزغ: سام أبرص لبياضه، والتبريص: الذي يلمع لمعان البرص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما in both clauses may be a relative noun, verbal-noun particle, or indefinite noun with adjective; only the noun options need a resumptive pronoun, unlike the particle for most grammarians.
rows.anchor: أن تكون موصولة اسمية أو حرفية أو نكرة موصوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four miraculous acts use imperfect verbs to signal that Jesus performed them repeatedly whenever asked.
rows.anchor: وأتى بهذه الخوارق الأربع بلفظ المضارع دلالة على تجدد ذلك كل وقت طلب منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation miracle is explicitly restricted to God’s permission because it is extraordinary and could suggest divinity; the healing clause omits the phrase.
rows.anchor: لأنه خارق عظيم، فأتى به دفعا لتوهم الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrection miracle is also restricted to God’s permission; the unqualified knowledge report signals its predecessor’s greatness and dispels mistaken divine attribution, which the author prefers over ellipsis of the qualifier.
rows.anchor: منبهة على عظم ما قبله ودفعا لوهم من يتوهم فيه الإلهية

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The general reading is تدخرون, from تذتخرون, an iftiʿāl form of ذخر meaning to hide or store; an anonymous poem uses ذخر for something stored, like الأكل for what is eaten.
rows.anchor: وأصله تذتخرون تفتعلون من الذخر وهو التخبئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the poem, ذخر is an action noun meaning the thing stored; some grammarians misread it as ووخز, and الثعالي and أرانيها mean foxes and rabbits.
rows.anchor: الذخر: فعل بمعنى المذخور نحو: الأكل بمعنى المأكول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound change from تذتخرون to تدخرون changes the form’s ت to د beside ذ, then assimilates ذ into د.
rows.anchor: أبدلت تاء الافتعال دالا مهملة فالتقى بذلك متقاربان: الذال والدال

rows.speaker: السوسي
rows.claim: Al-Susi, in a transmission from Abu ʿAmr, reads تذدخرون, changing ت to د without assimilation; it is permissible though assimilation is more eloquent.
rows.anchor: قرأ السوسي في رواية عن أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: الزهري ومجاهد وأبو السمال وأيوب السختياني
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri, Mujahid, Abu al-Sammal, and Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani read تذخرون, using the simple verb ذخرته, “I stored it”; Arabic also has ادخر with emphatic ذال.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري ومجاهد وأبو السمال وأيوب السختياني " تذخرون " بسكون الذال

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ gives an alternate derivation: تذتخرون changed ت to د to approach ذ, then ذ changed to د and assimilated; في بيوتكم attaches to تدخرون.
rows.anchor: والأصل في تدخرون: تذتخرون، إلا أن الذال مهجورة والتاء مهموسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: في بيوتكم attaches to تدخرون.
rows.anchor: " في بيوتكم " متعلق بتدخرون. قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذلك points to all the preceding miracles, using a singular demonstrative for a plural sense understood as everything mentioned; ʿAbd Allah’s reading has plural لآيات.
rows.anchor: وأشير إليها بلفظ الأفراد وإن كانت جمعا في المعنى

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: The ʿAbd Allah codex and reading have لآيات in the plural, reflecting the plural sense of the miracles.
rows.anchor: في مصحف عبد الله وقراءته: " لآيات " بالجمع مراعاة لما ذكرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing sentence may be spoken either by Jesus or by God.
rows.anchor: تحتمل أن تكون من كلام عيسى وأن تكون من كلام الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional apodosis is omitted: if they believe, they benefit from the sign and reflect on it.
rows.anchor: جوابه محذوف أي: إن كنتم مؤمنين انتفعتم بهذه الآية وتدبرتموها

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Sheikh proposes an omitted adjective, “beneficial,” for آية so the condition links to it; the author says no adjective is needed for that link.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " حتى يتجه التعلق بهذا الشرط "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Compared with the parallel in 2:83, this verse repeats ب before ذي القربى because it addresses this community, where kin deserve greater attention; repetition adds emphasis.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأنها في حق هذه الأمة فالاعتناء بها أكثر

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads إحسان in the nominative as subject with the preceding prepositional phrase as predicate; the statement expresses a command, like فصبر جميل in 12:18.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة " إحسان " بالرفع، على أنه مبتدأ

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority’s genitive الجار ذي القربى means a neighbor related by blood; الجار الجنب is a neighbor distant in lineage.
rows.anchor: المراد به القريب النسب، وبالجار الجنب البعيد النسب

rows.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
rows.claim: Maymun ibn Mihran interprets الجار ذي القربى as the nearby neighbor; Ibn ʿAtiyya calls this wrong because it combines ال with annexation, which should instead be جار ذي القربى.
rows.anchor: وعن ميمون بن مهران: " والجار ذي القربى أريد به الجار القريب "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author salvages Maymun’s sense by making ذي القربى an appositive with an omitted annexed noun, “neighbor of a kin-neighbor,” as in the cited Talha and علم الكبيرة examples.
rows.anchor: على حذف مضاف أي: والجار جار ذي القربى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some read الجار ذا القربى in the accusative; al-Zamakhshari parses it as an اختصاص construction, like الصلاة الوسطى in 2:238.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم: " والجار ذا القربى " نصبا. وخرجه الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جنب is an adjective on فعْل like ناقة سرح, invariant across gender and number; some speakers inflect it, as with شلل.
rows.anchor: يستوي فيه المفرد والمثنى والمجموع مذكرا ومؤنثا

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Asim reads الجنب with fatḥa on jim and a still nūn; it is an adjective meaning “neighboring,” like رجل عدل.
rows.anchor: وعن عاصم: " والجار الجنب " بفتح الجيم وسكون النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جنب derives from being at a side; its alif reflects wāw in تجاوروا and جاورته, it pluralizes as جيرة and جيران, and جنابة means distance, as the poem and 14:35 illustrate.
rows.anchor: لأن الإنسان يترك جانبا، ومنه: واجنبني وبني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In بالصاحب بالجنب, ب may mean “in” or retain its ordinary sense; the author prefers the ordinary sense, and either way it modifies الصاحب as a circumstantial phrase with an omitted governor.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن تكون بمعنى " في ". والثاني: أن تكون على بابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما ملكت أيمانكم may refer to owned kinds other than enslaved men and women, with ما used for types as in 4:3.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يريد غير العبيد والإماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ما encompasses all animals a person owns; ما is used because rational and nonrational kinds are mixed.
rows.anchor: وأن يكون أريد جميع ما ملكه الإنسان من الحيوانات
